rows.failed: A combined syntax-compilation and Git-status wrapper exceeded its 30-second bound without returning a result.
rows.passing: The isolated syntax compilation passed in 8.7 seconds, and the route builder independently admitted only its four declared starting paths.
rows.recovery: Split syntax compilation and Git-state inspection into separate bounded probes, crediting each only after its own successful result.
rows.recurrence_guard: Do not combine Python compilation and broad Windows Git status in one short wrapper; use separate bounds and outputs.

rows.failed: The first route build stripped the leading porcelain status column and misread an allowed scripts path as beginning with cripts.
rows.passing: The raw porcelain parser preserved all four declared starting paths and rejected no valid scripts or tests.
rows.recovery: Read git status --porcelain=v1 as raw captured output, preserve both status columns, and slice the path only after the fixed prefix.
rows.recurrence_guard: Never apply whole-output strip operations before parsing fixed-column Git porcelain records.

rows.failed: The second route build omitted the deliberately updated closeout compatibility test from its final correction allowlist and stopped before manifest creation.
rows.passing: The corrected allowlist admitted the compatibility test and all builder-owned phase artifacts while rejecting every unrelated path.
rows.recovery: Declare the closeout compatibility test as a route-correction path and permit only the builder's own phase artifacts during an idempotent retry from the unchanged closeout head.
rows.recurrence_guard: When a route correction changes a historical compatibility assertion, include that exact test in both starting and final path allowlists.

rows.failed: The idempotent retry reread the already-corrected working route and could not find the predecessor exact-title field.
rows.passing: The corrected builder resolved the superseded Ilyra route from the exact closeout object while keeping the new working route separate.
rows.recovery: Read predecessor route truth from the immutable closeout Git blob rather than from the mutable working tree.
rows.recurrence_guard: Bind every predecessor lifecycle read to its declared immutable commit whenever an additive correction may rerun.

rows.failed: The first correction test gate classified the newly created route-correction Method Flow files as mutations of the frozen closeout Method Flow domain.
rows.passing: The isolated seven-test correction module passed with the route Method Flow in scope and every frozen predecessor domain unchanged.
rows.recovery: Freeze inherited, evidence, and closeout Method Flow paths while explicitly admitting only route-correction-prefixed Method Flow artifacts in the additive correction.
rows.recurrence_guard: Define freeze domains by lifecycle ownership, not by a broad top-level directory prefix.

rows.failed: A bounded pre-commit wrapper assumed pytest was installed and stopped with No module named pytest before running any test.
rows.passing: The isolated closeout and route-correction unittest modules passed through Python's available standard-library test runner.
rows.recovery: Use the repository-native unittest module entrypoints already declared by the phase tests and final validator.
rows.recurrence_guard: Probe runner availability or use the repository-declared unittest entrypoint instead of assuming an optional pytest installation.
